security_frame.attacker: Later-stage Caliptra firmware (FMC or Runtime) executing at supervisor mode on the Caliptra microcontroller, after an earlier stage has provisioned a KeyVault slot that should be permanently locked for the remainder of the boot.
security_frame.precondition: A KeyVault entry holds key material that a policy says must be locked for use or for writes from a given boot stage onward, and no software has set that entry's KEY_CTRL.lock_use or KEY_CTRL.lock_wr bit.
security_frame.input: A KeyVault read or write request from a crypto engine whose dest_valid bit is set for that entry, plus AHB writes to the entry's KEY_CTRL register.
security_frame.protected_asset: KeyVault key material in a slot that a stage policy designates as locked, for example a DICE slot after the transition into FMC or Runtime.
security_frame.security_property: Lock enforcement and lock stickiness: an entry designated as locked must be unreadable or unwritable as the lock states, and once a lock bit is set it must not be clearable by software until the designated reset de-asserts.
security_frame.implemented_logic: src/keyvault/rtl/kv.sv:176-188 reads lock_wr and lock_use from the existing register values, qualifies them with ~fw_update_rst_window, and feeds them back as the swwel write-enable-low so a set lock suppresses further software writes to itself. src/keyvault/rtl/kv_reg.rdl:28-31 declares both fields as sw=rw; swwel=true; hw=r with resetsignal=core_only_rst_b, so no hwset, hw=w or we property exists and hardware has no path to set either bit. src/keyvault/rtl/kv.sv:233-234 makes lock_use_q suppress the read mux for every client, and src/keyvault/rtl/kv.sv:180-181 makes lock_wr_q and lock_use_q suppress the control write enable.

security_feature_bypassed: Boot-stage lock policy for KeyVault slots: the claim under test is that hardware must set lock_wr and lock_use on a stage transition through an hwset interface, with the hardware set taking priority over the software register value, and that this interface is absent.
proof_goal: Determine whether the KeyVault's lock enforcement and lock stickiness hold as the in-tree specification states, and whether the absence of a hardware set path for lock_wr and lock_use violates a requirement this design actually carries.
minimum_attack_sequence: An earlier boot stage provisions a KeyVault entry that a stage policy designates as locked from the next stage onward, and does not set that entry's lock bits.
The boot flow advances, and no hardware sets the lock bits because no hardware set path exists.
Later-stage firmware programs a crypto engine whose dest_valid bit is set to read the entry, or writes the entry through a write client.
The access succeeds where the stage policy says the slot should have been locked.
expected_evidence: A single-DUT simulation of the kv module that drives real AHB writes to KEY_CTRL, and measures: that setting lock_use suppresses the read for a client whose dest_valid bit is set; that a subsequent software write of zero to a set lock bit does not clear it; that setting lock_wr suppresses a write client and raises its write error; and what happens to a set lock bit across a core_only_rst_b pulse.

A structural audit that enumerates every hwset, we and hw=w property on the lock fields in the KeyVault register description, every driver of the lock fields in the RTL, every boot-stage-like signal in the tree that could key a hardware set, and the in-tree specification statements about who sets the lock bits and when they clear.
success_criteria: The claim is upheld only if BOTH the simulation shows a lock enforcement or lock stickiness property failing AND the audit identifies an in-tree requirement that HARDWARE set the lock bits, together with a stage-transition signal that reaches or could reach the kv module.

If the simulation shows lock enforcement and stickiness holding as docs/CaliptraHardwareSpecification.md:2459-2460 states, and the in-tree specifications assign lock setting to ROM or firmware rather than to hardware, then the claim is withdrawn and the case is recorded as false_alarm: the absent hwset interface is not a required hardware feature of this design.

Pre-committed withdrawal: the mere absence of an hwset property in the register description will not be reported as a defect on its own. A missing hardware set path is a defect only if some in-tree statement requires hardware to perform the set, or some in-tree logic attempts the set and is silently dropped.
non_findings_intent: Suspected but unproven at plan time: that the in-tree specification requires hardware to set the lock bits on a stage transition. To be checked against docs/CaliptraHardwareSpecification.md:2455-2461, src/keyvault/config/keyvault.md and the integration specification; to be withdrawn if those documents describe the lock bits as microcontroller-set.

Suspected but unproven at plan time: that some module in the tree drives a lock set that the register description silently discards, which would be a real broken connection. To be checked by enumerating every assignment to the lock fields in the RTL; to be withdrawn if the only writers are the swwel feedback and the software register interface.

To be measured, with the verdict deferred to what the in-tree documents say rather than decided in advance: the state of a set lock bit after a core_only_rst_b pulse, given that src/keyvault/rtl/kv_reg.rdl:28-31 names core_only_rst_b as the lock fields' resetsignal while the key data fields at src/keyvault/rtl/kv_reg.rdl:22 reset on hard_reset_b. If a set lock clears there while the key data persists, the plan will record the measurement and identify precisely which in-tree sentence would have to be violated for it to be a defect, rather than asserting one.
